selectionPrinciples: Favor broadly useful agents that help on real software delivery work across many repos.
Prefer agents with clear scopes, strong operating instructions, and low persona fluff.
Balance implementers, reviewers, debuggers, and orchestration roles so the set works as a starter kit.
Keep a bias toward agents that are easy to delegate to from a parent agent inside a live project.

agents.whyPicked: The best all-around safety net in the repo. It gives you a disciplined second pass on correctness, regressions, security, and missing tests.
agents.watchFor: Works best on a bounded feature path, diff, or incident area rather than an entire repo with no scope.

agents.whyPicked: A strong default implementation agent for production backend work, with good attention to auth, failure paths, and persistence boundaries.
agents.watchFor: Best after the owning service path is known. Pair it with code-mapper when the repo is unfamiliar.

agents.whyPicked: A high-value agent when something is broken and the shortest path is evidence-driven isolation rather than speculative fixing.
agents.watchFor: Its value is highest when you can give it logs, traces, failing tests, or a reproducible symptom.

agents.whyPicked: This is the best uncertainty-reduction agent in the set. It helps you find entry points, ownership boundaries, and blast radius before you edit.
agents.watchFor: It is intentionally non-creative. Use it for mapping first, then hand off to an implementation or review agent.

agents.whyPicked: Useful well beyond formal audits. It gives a focused security pass on auth, secrets, validation, and exposure surfaces.
agents.watchFor: It does static review well, but environment-level verification still matters for full confidence.

agents.whyPicked: A practical default for production UI work because it balances behavior, state integrity, accessibility, and design-system alignment.
agents.watchFor: It is better for scoped UI delivery than broad redesign or visual exploration.

agents.whyPicked: A good vertical-slice agent when a change crosses UI, API, and persistence and you want one owner with end-to-end accountability.
agents.watchFor: It is most effective on a coherent feature path, not on repo-wide cleanups or architecture resets.

agents.whyPicked: A strong companion agent for shipping safely. It pushes toward deterministic, risk-targeted coverage instead of broad test churn.
agents.watchFor: It is best when paired with a known defect, changed behavior, or a clearly risky integration edge.

agents.whyPicked: One of the most broadly useful language specialists because so many app repos lean on TypeScript for runtime contracts and refactors.
agents.watchFor: Its best work comes from matching types to runtime truth, not from cosmetic type churn.

agents.whyPicked: A versatile specialist for service code, scripts, internal tooling, and data-adjacent workflows in Python-heavy repos.
agents.watchFor: Use it when Python is clearly the owning path rather than as a generic fallback for any backend work.

agents.whyPicked: Great for slowing down just enough before implementation. It helps keep APIs explicit, stable, and migration-aware.
agents.watchFor: Use it before coding or during contract changes; it is not meant to implement the service itself.

agents.whyPicked: One of the best operational agents in the repo, with a strong bias toward safe pipelines, rollback clarity, and deterministic delivery.
agents.watchFor: It shines when there is a concrete pipeline, deployment path, or environment issue to improve.

agents.whyPicked: A high-signal specialist for modern React repos where component boundaries, rendering behavior, and async state patterns really matter.
agents.watchFor: Use it when the owning UI path is clearly React; otherwise the broader frontend agent is safer.

agents.whyPicked: A practical choice for Node-based APIs and toolchains where event-loop behavior, package ecosystem conventions, and runtime details matter.
agents.watchFor: It is most useful when the problem is truly Node-specific rather than generic backend logic.

agents.whyPicked: A valuable specialist whenever performance, correctness, or reporting issues come down to query shape and data boundaries.
agents.watchFor: It is best used for query and contract analysis, often alongside the owning application agent.

agents.whyPicked: A focused agent for real bottlenecks, not vague tuning. It encourages measurement, dominant-cost targeting, and explicit tradeoffs.
agents.watchFor: Give it evidence such as traces, timings, benchmarks, or a clear slow path whenever possible.

agents.whyPicked: Especially relevant if you want to systematize agent workflows. It is one of the few agents explicitly shaped around tool contracts and MCP integration.
agents.watchFor: It is specialized. Use it when the task involves MCP servers, clients, schemas, or protocol-aware integrations.

agents.whyPicked: A useful grounding agent when you want trustworthy docs that match the actual repo and operator workflow rather than generic prose.
agents.watchFor: It works best when there is a concrete workflow boundary to document or repair.

agents.whyPicked: Worth keeping around because it is intentionally narrow. When a UI defect is already reproduced, this one stays disciplined and ships the smallest safe patch.
agents.watchFor: Use it for tight repair work, not for feature development or design exploration.

agents.whyPicked: This is a good 'adult supervision' agent for larger repo-wide changes. It is cautious, explicit about risk, and useful when you want proposal-first governance.
agents.watchFor: It is for analysis and gating, not autonomous editing. Pair it with implementation agents after approval.
